Astonied
uh-STON-eed
adjective / verb (archaic past)
Older English for astonished: struck senseless with wonder, fear, or grief; used of Nebuchadnezzar, Daniel, and the vision of the Servant.

📖 Biblical Definition

Astonied is the Authorized Version’s older form of astonished: the mind struck as if to stone by what it sees. Nebuchadnezzar was astonied when he saw four men loose in the fire. Daniel was astonied for one hour at the king’s dream. Isaiah says many were astonied at the Servant, His visage so marred more than any man. The word is not light surprise. It is the halt of human composure before the acts and sufferings of God’s purpose. Empires are astonied by deliverance they did not decree. Prophets are astonied by visions that outrun their strength. The nations are astonied at a Redeemer who saves by being marred. Modern English softened the form; it must not soften the meaning. Holy history should still leave the church astonied—not with unbelief, but with worship. A faith that never stops short in awe has not yet looked hard at the furnace, the dream, or the cross. The same Lord who astonishes kings still humbles the proud by mercy and by judgment in the sight of all flesh. Better a church astonied before the cross than a church amused by everything else.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Struck with overwhelming wonder or dread; archaic form of astonished used in Daniel and Isaiah for holy shock.

expand to see more

ASTONIED, astonished; confounded with wonder or fear.

Nebuchadnezzar was astonied at the fourth man in the fire.

Daniel was astonied by the heavy vision of the king.

Many were astonied at the marred visage of the Servant.

The word marks holy shock, not casual surprise.

📖 Key Scripture

Dan 3:24 — "Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors, Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire? They answered and said unto the king, True, O king."

Dan 4:19 — "Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was astonied for one hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king spake, and said, Belteshazzar, let not the dream, or the interpretation thereof, trouble thee. Belteshazzar answered and said, My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies."

Isa 52:14 — "As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men:"

Act 9:6 — "And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A culture of constant stimulation is seldom astonied at God; Scripture records men stopped cold by His works and by Christ’s marring.

expand to see more

The corruption is jaded unbelief that yawns at miracle and passion alike. Furnace, dream, and cross become content. Another corruption is theatrical shock without repentance—astonishment as entertainment. Biblical being astonied leads to confession, decree, or prophetic burden. When the church recovers that, she will preach a Christ who still stops the mouth, not a brand that never startles.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition of the archaic form itself. What must be recovered is the capacity for reverent awe before the works of God and the sufferings of the Servant, against an age that is shocked by everything except holiness.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Astonied means struck with awe or dread; Scripture applies it to kings, prophets, and onlookers of the marred Servant.

expand to see more

English — astonied, older astonished.

Daniel — king and prophet both astonied.

Isaiah — many astonied at the Servant’s marring.

Sense — mind halted before divine act or grief.

Worship — awe that should end in faith, not cynicism.

Usage

"Nebuchadnezzar was astonied at the men in the fire."

"Daniel was astonied at the dream’s burden."

"Many were astonied at the marred visage of Christ the Servant."
